title: European Air War Atlas campaign evidence audit
notes: Dates are inclusive reporting dates. A month-level interval identifies the available scope when day cutoffs cannot be assigned safely.

Rows preserve the source's reporting force, geography, category and phase. Overlapping rows and component/total lines can describe the same aircraft. Use the scope and row metadata before aggregating.

Claims, aircraft missing, damage, write-offs, serviceable stock and sorties have distinct metrics. Omitted values are unknown. Explicit zeros or reconciled accounting dashes are explained by the series scope.

Recorded means a wartime observation in a report or reproduction. Source-compiled means an identified historical compilation or transcription. Secondary reconstruction means a later account, including institutional histories. Confidence refers to fidelity to the identified passage and scope; it does not validate a claimant's estimate or independently match an enemy loss.
